data.description:
# Detect stranded in-progress children

Parent: **SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN**.

## Target outcome

`drive`/`parent` name the stranded child instead of silently leaving it `in-progress` and blocking `wl next`: a child whose session died after pushing work is reported with its pushed-commit evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Stranded check.** A child whose session failed while the item is non-terminal is checked for stranded work using git evidence against `origin/dev` (e.g. `git -C <worktree> log origin/dev --grep <child-id>`, or `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> origin/dev`) (parent AC3).
- **Read-only detection.** Detection performs no `wl` mutation and no worktree mutation (parent constraint).
- **Clear diagnostic.** The drive report carries `stranded_children` (id, status, stage, commit evidence) and a worklog comment on the parent names the stranded item and how to finalise it (parent AC3).
- **Graceful degradation.** Git unavailable, no remote, or an unreadable worktree degrades to "unknown" without crashing and without false positives (parent AC2, AC3).
- **Tests from the stranded-detection test suite pass** (parent AC5).

### Parent AC coverage (traceability)

- Covers parent AC-2: **Non-terminal children still fail hard.** When a driven child's session times out and the child is **not** terminal, the existing hard-failure behaviour is preserved (report fails the child, stops the chain) — regression-guarded.
- Covers parent AC-3: **Stranded in-progress children are detected and finalised.** A child whose work was pushed to `dev` but whose item is still `in-progress` after its session is killed (missing terminal update) is detected at the next `phase_parent`/`drive` pass and finalised to `completed`/`in_review` (or a clear diagnostic is emitted naming the stranded item) — the item must not remain an orphaned `in-progress` blocking `wl next`.
- Covers parent AC-5: **Tests pass.** Existing tests for `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` continue to pass; new tests cover the timeout-reconciliation paths (unit tests in the implement-skill test suite).
## Definition of done

- Stranded detection implemented and reported; tests from the detection test item pass; existing drive/parent tests green.

## Minimal implementation

- Add helper `_detect_stranded_child(child_id, worktree_path, parent_branch) -> dict` returning `{stranded: bool, commit: str, evidence: str, reason: str}`; evidence provider injectable for tests.
- Call it from `phase_drive` on the non-terminal spawn-failure path (after reconciliation fails) and add the result to the report.
- Emit one `wl` comment per drive invocation on the parent (never per iteration) naming stranded children.

## Constraints

- Read-only: no `StatusLifecycle` call in this item.
- Bound git calls (single `git log --grep` + optional ancestry check), only on the failure path.
- Keep session-per-child isolation and worktree semantics unchanged.

## Risky assumptions

- The child's commit message or branch ancestry reliably links the pushed commit to the child id (the implement workflow commits reference the work-item id).
- A stale local `origin/dev` ref is acceptable evidence; fetch is out of scope (avoid network on the failure path).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the stranded-detection test suite item.

## Deliverables

- `_detect_stranded_child`, drive wiring, and parent worklog diagnostic.

data.description:
# Finalise stranded children safely

Parent: **SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN**.

## Target outcome

A stranded child (work pushed to `dev`, item still `in-progress` after its session was killed) is finalised through the existing `StatusLifecycle` path when the evidence is unambiguous, so it no longer blocks `wl next`; otherwise the detection diagnostic from the previous item stands.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Guarded finalisation.** When the child is `in-progress`, its commit is verified on `origin/dev`, and its worktree holds no uncommitted work, `drive` finalises the child to `completed`/`in_review` through the existing `StatusLifecycle` path so it no longer blocks `wl next` (parent AC3).
- **Never unsafe.** Finalisation never runs when evidence is missing, never for a child claimed by another live agent, and never discards uncommitted work (parent AC3, constraint).
- **Recorded.** A worklog comment on the child and on the parent records the evidence (status/stage/commit) and why the item was finalised automatically (parent AC3, AC4).
- **Fallback.** When no safe finalise path is available the behaviour falls back to the read-only diagnostic from the detection item (parent AC3).
- **Tests from the stranded-detection test suite pass**, including the read-only-default case (parent AC5).

### Parent AC coverage (traceability)

- Covers parent AC-3: **Stranded in-progress children are detected and finalised.** A child whose work was pushed to `dev` but whose item is still `in-progress` after its session is killed (missing terminal update) is detected at the next `phase_parent`/`drive` pass and finalised to `completed`/`in_review` (or a clear diagnostic is emitted naming the stranded item) — the item must not remain an orphaned `in-progress` blocking `wl next`.
- Covers parent AC-4: **Drive report distinguishes timeout outcomes.** The per-child `children_driven` entry or failure reason distinguishes "timed out but child completed" from "timed out, child incomplete" with the terminal evidence (status/stage/commit) so the report is truthful.
- Covers parent AC-5: **Tests pass.** Existing tests for `phase_drive`/`phase_parent` continue to pass; new tests cover the timeout-reconciliation paths (unit tests in the implement-skill test suite).
## Definition of done

- Opt-in/evidence-gated finalisation implemented, tests green, and a worklog audit trail written for every automatic finalisation.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `_finalise_stranded_child(child_id, evidence) -> dict` using `StatusLifecycle.update_status(child_id, "completed", stage="in_review")` plus a child comment.
- Gate it behind an explicit drive option (e.g. `--finalise-stranded`) and the evidence checks from `_detect_stranded_child`.
- Call it from `phase_drive` on the stranded path after detection succeeds; record the outcome in the report (`finalised_children`).

## Constraints

- Mutation only via the existing `StatusLifecycle` finalise path (parent constraint: no other `wl` mutation).
- Do not discard, stash, or commit worktree contents.
- Do not re-spawn a session for a finalised child.

## Risky assumptions

- The `StatusLifecycle` write reaches the main worklog store — known open defect SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL ("finish reports status changes that the main worklog store does not show"); if it is unresolved, prefer the diagnostic and record the limitation.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the stranded in-progress detection item.

## Deliverables

- `_finalise_stranded_child`, drive option + wiring, tests, and audit comments.
data.title: Finalise stranded children safely

data.description:
Discovered by a full-project `/skill:refactor` scan of this repository (499 source files, clean `dev` checkout).

## User Story

**As a** producer running a refactor scan,
**I want** the report's "Auto-fixed" count to reflect changes actually written to disk,
**so that** I can trust the report and do not believe lint debt was cleaned when the tree is
byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Observed behaviour

`python3 skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` (no work-item id) reported:

```
Auto-fix applied 9 fixes via linters on 437 files
Auto-fixed:     9
Remaining smells: 9
```

but `git status` showed **no** source-file changes (only a pre-existing modification to
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), and a follow-up check confirmed the same 9 diagnostics
are still present:

```
$ ruff check --select SIM102,EXE005,ISC004,SIM115,UP031,SIM117,EXE001 \
    skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py skill/implement/scripts/implement.py \
    skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py \
    tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py
Found 9 errors.
No fixes available (3 hidden fixes can be enabled with the `--unsafe-fixes` option).
```

The same 9 findings are then also listed under "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)", i.e. they are
counted twice: once as fixed, once as outstanding.

## Root cause (suspected)

`_parse_ruff_fix_output()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` turns **every** JSON entry emitted by
`ruff check --fix --output-format json` into a "fixed finding". Ruff's JSON output after `--fix`
contains the diagnostics that **remain** (those it could not or would not fix, e.g. EXE005/EXE001
shebang/exec bit rules and unsafe-fix candidates), not a ledger of applied fixes. Findings with a
null `fix` field should not be counted as applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output()` should be checked for the same assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` / `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` count a finding as fixed only when the
   linter actually applied a fix (e.g. ruff entry carries a non-null `fix` payload, or fixes are
   detected by comparing file content before/after the run).
2. A regression test proves that a linter run over files whose remaining diagnostics are
   non-fixable reports `fixes_applied: false` / `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A full-project scan of a clean tree leaves `git status` unchanged **and** reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
4. The "Remaining smells" list is not a duplicate of the auto-fixed list for the same diagnostics.
data.title: Refactor skill reports unfixed linter diagnostics as applied auto-fixes

data.comment: Completed work pushed to dev, see commit 75d0c3f48. Adds _git_commit_evidence (read-only git log --grep <child-id> against origin/dev then dev, 30s bound, graceful None on missing worktree/git error/no ref) and _detect_stranded_child (injectable commit_evidence provider, degrades to unknown, never raises, never a false positive). phase_drive gains a commit_evidence parameter: on the non-terminal spawn-failure path it emits stranded_children entries (id/status/stage/commit/evidence/reason), marks the entry stranded with commit_evidence, and posts exactly ONE parent worklog comment per drive invocation naming each stranded item and how to finalise it -- no status mutation. Removed the four xfail markers from TestStrandedChildren (now passing) and made every drive test hermetic by patching wl_add_comment. Full suite green at 75d0c3f48 (803 node tests + pytest, 0 failures).
